decision: set the definition of done as a falsifiable predicate covering the published url, the loud failure, and the idempotent second run
why: the whole point of this product is that both prior attempts never published anything, so the finish line has to be a url and a second run that does nothing

decision: set rigor high on the publish spine and medium on the curator logic
why: the spine is a one-way door that is cheap to settle now and expensive to settle later, and the curator is fully reversible

decision: found that harness.root ignores its agent option when the root already exists
why: the existing src/harness.ts looked like it applied the model on every run and does not, so a provider change would silently never take effect

decision: found that pi-durable has no public way to enumerate a document family
why: any design that needs to list seen articles has to own a key index, which pushed the seen-set decision

decision: found that the designed publish chain had no build step and mixed two branches
why: the publisher wrote content on master while Pages served main, and nothing rebuilt dist, so a successful publish would have left the site stale

decision: picked candidate A as the base and candidate B as the donor
why: A had the coherent attempt and failure state, the correct request-identifier resume, and the only credible seen-set

decision: grafted B's reference-only answer shape and angle-bracket link destinations onto A
why: A asked the model for a summary and a reason and rendered links as (url), which a feed-controlled url can break out of

decision: rejected B's absence of an article-level seen-set
why: B dissolves the question, which leaves a story that appears on two feeds on two days published twice
evidence: openspec/changes/add-slopchop-newsletter/design.md, The seen-set belongs to the published artifact

decision: reproduced that a javascript link survives contentlayer's markdown pipeline unchanged
why: the earlier measurement that raw html is dropped had been read as safety, and it says nothing about link schemes

decision: reproduced that a url containing a closing parenthesis is truncated when written as a markdown destination
why: this is a content-integrity bug on a page under the author's name, not a theoretical one

decision: resolved the quiet-day question by stating a default instead of leaving it open
why: the task instruction says an open question that changes what gets built has to be resolved first, and the change is one branch in the renderer if the owner wants the other behaviour

decision: sequenced the artifact first and the curator second
why: both prior attempts built a pipeline and never shipped a page, so the page has to exist before the pipeline is worth building

decision: moved the arena artifacts into the repository so the trail's evidence resolves after the run
why: two rows pointed at /tmp paths that will not survive, and the audit checks that every evidence pointer resolves

decision: recorded the design's provenance: the two arena candidates and the grounding they were given
why: a reviewer deciding whether the synthesis was right needs the candidates, not only the conclusion
